name: Food trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about dishes, ingredients, cuisines, cooking terms. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: When Escoffier revised Carême's list of foundational sauces, which sauce did he demote to a derivative of velouté?
items.explain: Carême listed allemande as a mother sauce, but Escoffier treated it as a derivative of velouté and put hollandaise in its place.

source.title: French Cuisine's 5 Mother Sauces, Explained - Tasting Table

items.question: Which mother sauce, whose name means 'velvet', is made by combining a light roux with a clear white stock?
items.explain: Velouté is a light roux thickened with clear or white stock. Béchamel uses milk instead.

source.title: French Cuisine's 5 Mother Sauces, Explained - Tasting Table

items.question: In which 1903 cookbook did Auguste Escoffier set out his five mother sauces?
items.explain: Escoffier presented his refined list of mother sauces in Le Guide Culinaire (1903), adding hollandaise and tomato and treating allemande as a velouté derivative.

source.title: French sauces: Learn the 5 mother sauces, uses & techniques

items.question: Which classic 'daughter' sauce is made by further reducing espagnole, the brown mother sauce?
items.explain: Reducing espagnole further, sometimes with wine, sherry or Madeira added, gives demi-glace.

items.question: In Wilbur Scoville's original 1912 organoleptic test, pepper extract was diluted in what until tasters could no longer detect heat?
items.explain: The extract was diluted in sugar water, and the degree of dilution at which a panel could no longer detect heat gave the Scoville rating.

items.question: Wilbur Scoville devised his famous heat scale in 1912 while working for which pharmaceutical company?
items.explain: Scoville devised the test in 1912 while working at Parke-Davis, to measure the pungency of chili peppers.

items.question: Which compound, found in a cactus-like plant from Morocco, rates around 15 billion on the Scoville scale?
items.explain: The Scoville scale can also rate other pungent compounds, and resiniferatoxin measures around 15 billion SHU.

source.title: How Do You Measure the 'Heat' of a Pepper? - NIST

items.question: Scoville originally created his test to measure capsaicin for use in which kind of product?
items.explain: The scale began as a pharmaceutical tool for gauging the capsaicin in salves used for muscle pain, not as a culinary measure.

source.title: The Spicy Legacy of Alum Wilbur Scoville - MCPHS

items.question: Which temperature range is commonly cited for the Maillard browning reaction in cooking?
items.explain: The Maillard reaction is usually cited as occurring at about 140–165°C (280–330°F). At higher temperatures caramelization takes over.

items.question: Which sugar is NOT a reducing sugar in its usual form, so it does not directly take part in Maillard browning?
items.explain: Glucose and fructose are reducing sugars that react with amino compounds. Table sugar (sucrose) is not a reducing sugar in its usual form.

source.title: Maillard reaction in food manufacturing - Ragus Sugars

items.question: What name is given to the brown pigments produced by the Maillard reaction?
items.explain: The Maillard reaction produces brown pigments called melanoidins, which give roasted and baked foods their colour and savory flavours.

source.title: How to Explain the Maillard Reaction

items.question: Which part of the Crocus sativus flower is dried to make saffron?
items.explain: Saffron is made from the dried, pollen-receiving stigmas of the flower, three per bloom.

items.question: Roughly how many saffron crocus flowers are needed to yield one gram of dried saffron?
items.explain: Each flower gives only three tiny stigmas, so about 150 flowers are needed per gram of dried spice. This is why saffron is so expensive.

source.title: Saffron - UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County

items.question: Which toxic, fall-flowering plant, sometimes called 'meadow saffron', must not be confused with the saffron crocus?
items.explain: Colchicums look similar to the saffron crocus but are toxic. They have six stamens, while true crocuses have three.

source.title: Saffron - UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County

items.question: Under PDO rules, what is the minimum maturation period for Parmigiano Reggiano?
items.explain: Parmigiano Reggiano must mature for at least 12 months within its area of origin before it can be sold.

source.title: What makes Parmigiano Reggiano Pdo unique - Italianfood.net

items.question: Parmigiano Reggiano's production area lies between which two Italian rivers?
items.explain: The area covers Parma, Reggio Emilia, Modena, and parts of Mantua and Bologna, between the Po and Reno rivers.

source.title: Parmigiano Reggiano, characteristics and nutritional values - Agriform

items.question: A 1612 document from which Duke of Parma marks the start of efforts to protect Parmigiano Reggiano from counterfeits?
items.explain: The history of protecting the cheese's designation of origin is traced to a 1612 document of Ranuccio Farnese, Duke of Parma.

source.title: Parmigiano Reggiano DOP - Wine and Travel Italy

items.question: The word 'mole' derives from the Nahuatl chilmolli. What does that word mean?
items.explain: In Nahuatl, 'chil' means chilli pepper and 'molli' means sauce or ragout.

items.question: What is a dried poblano pepper called?
items.explain: A fresh poblano becomes a chile ancho when dried. The pasilla is sometimes wrongly called 'poblano' but is a different pepper.

items.question: According to legend, nuns of which convent in Puebla created mole poblano to honour a visiting archbishop?
items.explain: The story says a nun at the Santa Rosa convent made the sauce for Juan de Palafox, Viceroy of New Spain and Archbishop of Puebla. The origin is disputed.

items.question: Which umami compound does katsuobushi mainly contribute to dashi?
items.explain: Kombu supplies glutamic acid, while katsuobushi and niboshi supply inosinic acid.

source.title: Dashi: Japanese Soup Stock Guide & Easy Recipe

items.question: In Japanese cooking, what is 'niban dashi'?
answers: A stock made by reusing the first batch's solids
A vegan stock made only from dried shiitake
A stock of dried sardines simmered for hours
A syrupy stock reduced to a thick glaze
items.correct: A stock made by reusing the first batch's solids
items.explain: Niban ('second') dashi is made by reusing the kombu and katsuobushi left over from the first dashi. It has a milder aroma than ichiban dashi.

items.question: What distinguishes the salt traditionally used to brine napa cabbage for baechu-kimchi?
answers: It has a larger grain than kitchen salt
It is milled as fine as table salt
It is infused with rice vinegar
items.correct: It has a larger grain than kitchen salt
items.explain: Korean brining salt has a larger grain size than common kitchen salt, and it is used for the initial salting of the cabbage.

items.question: Which ingredient, first imported during Korea's Joseon Dynasty, quickly became widespread as a kimchi seasoning?
items.explain: Chili peppers arrived in Korea during the Joseon Dynasty and soon became a standard seasoning for kimchi.

source.title: Kimchi—Fermented Korean Napa Cabbage - Chefs Society

items.question: In what year did 11 Marseille restaurateurs draw up the Bouillabaisse Charter?
items.explain: In 1980, 11 Marseille restaurateurs drew up a charter codifying both the ingredients and the method of preparing bouillabaisse.

items.question: Bouillabaisse is said to have roots in an ancient Greek fish soup called what?
items.explain: Provençal sources trace bouillabaisse to the Greek kakavia, which is said to date from the founding of Marseille in the 7th century BC.

items.question: The name of rouille, the garlicky sauce served with bouillabaisse, translates from French as what?
items.explain: Rouille means 'rust', after the sauce's reddish colour.

source.title: The Story of Bouillabaisse - Perfectly Provence

items.question: Which French chef pioneered sous vide cooking at the Troisgros restaurant in the 1970s, combining vacuum sealing with low-temperature cooking?
items.explain: Georges Pralus pioneered cooking vacuum-sealed food at low temperature in the 1970s and is often called the father of sous vide.

source.title: A Brief History of Sous Vide - Suvie

items.question: Which American-born physicist described low-and-slow cooking in 1799, an early ancestor of sous vide?
items.explain: Benjamin Thompson (Count Rumford) described low-temperature cooking in 1799, long before modern vacuum-sealed sous vide.

source.title: A Brief History of Sous Vide - Suvie

items.question: Which ingredient is typical of Western-style curry powder but absent from garam masala?
items.explain: Garam masala uses no turmeric and is sweeter, leaning on spices such as cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg or mace.

source.title: Garam Masala Recipe - The Daring Gourmet

items.question: Tempering chocolate aims to build which form of cocoa butter crystal?
items.explain: Form V crystals are the key to good chocolate. They are not the most stable form (that is Form VI), but they give snap and gloss.

items.question: At roughly what temperature does the Form V cocoa butter crystal melt?
items.explain: Type V cocoa butter melts at about 33.8°C (92.8°F), so tempered chocolate must be worked below that.

source.title: Tempering - Deconstruction and Reconstruction - Chocolate Alchemy

items.question: Which Beijing roast-duck restaurant brand was founded in 1864?
items.explain: Quanjude was established in 1864 and is famous for its Peking duck. Bianyifang is much older, dating from the 1410s.

items.question: Quanjude's roast-duck tradition uses non-smoky hardwood from which kind of tree to give a subtle fruity flavour?
items.explain: Quanjude's open-oven roasting uses non-smoky fruitwoods such as Chinese date (jujube), peach or pear.

items.question: In what year was the Pekin duck breed introduced to the United States from China?
items.explain: The Pekin breed, now a common choice for roast duck, was introduced to the U.S. from China in 1873.

source.title: A Brief History of Peking Duck - Modern Farmer

items.question: Which Tokyo Imperial University chemist identified glutamate as the source of kombu's savoury taste in 1908 and named that taste 'umami'?
items.explain: Ikeda analysed kombu dashi, isolated the glutamate responsible for its flavour, and coined the word 'umami' in 1908.

items.question: What is the minimum ageing period for the standard 'Affinato' grade of Traditional Balsamic Vinegar of Modena PDO?
items.explain: The product specification sets 'Affinato' at a minimum of 12 years, while 'Extravecchio' needs at least 25 years.

items.question: In nixtamalization, dried maize kernels are cooked and steeped in water with which alkaline compound?
items.explain: Nixtamalization uses food-grade lime, which is calcium hydroxide. It loosens the kernel's outer skin and raises the calcium content of the masa.

items.question: In Roman fish-sauce production, what was the paste left behind after the liquid garum was drawn off called?
items.explain: Garum was the thick amber liquid from fermented fish guts and salt. The paste left behind was called allec, an inferior product that was also widely traded.

source.title: What Is Garum? More About Rome's Funky Sauce Made of Fish Guts

items.question: Which Neapolitan pizzaiolo is traditionally credited with creating pizza Margherita in 1889 in honour of a visiting queen?
items.explain: The Royal Palace of Capodimonte commissioned Raffaele Esposito to make a pizza for Queen Margherita, and the Margherita is the result.

items.question: Sichuan pepper, famous for its numbing tingle, belongs to which plant family?
items.explain: Sichuan pepper comes from the genus Zanthoxylum in the family Rutaceae. It is not closely related to black pepper or chili pepper.

items.question: On which Indian Ocean island did a 12-year-old enslaved boy, Edmond Albius, devise a practical method of hand-pollinating vanilla in 1841?
items.explain: Albius worked on the French island of Réunion. His hand-pollination technique let vanilla be grown commercially outside Mexico.

items.question: The French stew cassoulet takes its name from which item?
answers: The cassis, a blackcurrant cordial used to glaze the crust
The cassoun, an Occitan word for the white haricot bean
The casse, a Languedoc term for slow-rendered goose fat
The cassole, the hollow earthenware dish it is cooked in
items.correct: The cassole, the hollow earthenware dish it is cooked in
items.explain: The dish is named after the cassole, the hollow terracotta cooking dish traditionally used to make it.

items.question: Traditional Ethiopian injera, a sour, spongy fermented flatbread, is made from the flour of which grain?
items.explain: Injera is traditionally made from teff flour. Teff is a cereal crop that originated in Ethiopia.

items.question: Under EU law, Roquefort may only be aged in the natural caves of which mountain at Roquefort-sur-Soulzon?
items.explain: Roquefort has protected designation of origin status. Only cheeses aged in the natural Combalou caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon may carry the name.

items.question: What is the main force that puffs up pâte à choux, the dough for éclairs and cream puffs, as it bakes?
answers: Air whipped into beaten egg whites
Wild yeast from a long fermentation
items.explain: Choux relies on steam leavening. The water in the paste turns to steam in the hot oven and inflates the dough.

items.question: What is the Spanish name for the autumn-to-winter season when Iberian pigs fatten on acorns in the dehesa?
items.explain: The montanera, roughly October to February, is when Iberian pigs gain much of their weight on acorns. Acorn feeding during it is what earns the 'de bellota' label.

source.title: The story behind jamón ibérico de bellota

items.question: In San Francisco-style sourdough, maltose-negative yeasts live alongside Fructilactobacillus sanfranciscensis. Which sugar does the bacterium need that the yeast cannot use?
items.explain: The yeast cannot metabolise the maltose in the dough, but the bacterium requires it. This lets the two microbes share the dough without competing for it.

items.question: Which sour fruit pulp, used alongside anchovies, is a signature ingredient of Worcestershire sauce?
items.explain: Worcestershire sauce is built on vinegar, anchovies and tamarind, among other ingredients. The tamarind gives it a fruity tartness.

items.question: Which mould, known in Japan as kōji-kin, is the fermentation workhorse behind sake, miso and soy sauce?
items.explain: Aspergillus oryzae is the kōji mould used to make sake, miso, soy sauce and other traditional Japanese foods. Its enzymes break down starches and proteins.
